title: Physical Chemistry I (Thermodynamics & Statistical Mechanics)
description: Develop a molecularly grounded command of chemical thermodynamics and statistical mechanics, so students can predict phase behavior, solution behavior, chemical equilibrium, electrochemical work, and thermodynamic properties from both data and molecular models.

topics.title: Thermodynamic Systems, States, and Equations of State
topics.description: This opening unit defines the language of macroscopic thermodynamics: systems, surroundings, state variables, paths, and equations of state.

children.title: Systems and state variables
children.description: Students learn what is being modeled before calculating energy, entropy, or equilibrium.

children.title: Equations of state
children.description: Equations of state connect measurable variables and reveal when ideal models break down.

children.title: Van der Waals and virial equations
Thermodynamic processes
children.description: Process language helps students interpret experiments and reversible/irreversible limits.

topics.title: First Law of Thermodynamics
topics.description: The first law is conservation of energy written for chemical systems, connecting heat, work, internal energy, and measurable changes.

children.title: Internal energy and energy accounting
children.description: Students learn to track energy without confusing heat and work with stored energy.

children.title: Pressure-volume work
children.description: PV work is the simplest route from mechanical models to thermodynamic processes.

children.title: Heat capacities
children.description: Heat capacities translate temperature changes into energy changes.

topics.title: Enthalpy and Thermochemistry
topics.description: Enthalpy makes chemistry's heat effects practical because many reactions occur at constant pressure.

children.title: Reaction enthalpy
children.description: Students learn how heat of reaction is defined, measured, and related to molecular change.

children.title: Hess's law
children.description: Thermochemical cycles show that state functions allow indirect calculations.

children.title: Phase-change energetics
children.description: Phase transitions provide concrete examples of latent heat and molecular interactions.

topics.title: Second Law, Entropy, and Irreversibility
topics.description: The second law explains directionality: why some processes happen spontaneously and why energy quality matters.

children.title: Entropy change
children.description: Students learn entropy as a state function tied to heat flow and multiplicity.

children.title: Irreversible processes
children.description: Irreversibility links real processes to entropy production.

children.title: Second-law statements
children.description: Different statements of the second law reveal the same physical constraint.

topics.title: Free Energy, Spontaneity, and Thermodynamic Potentials
topics.description: Free energies translate the first and second laws into criteria for chemical change under common laboratory constraints.

children.title: Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies
children.description: Students learn which potential is minimized under which conditions.

children.title: Legendre transforms
children.description: Legendre transforms explain why different potentials use different natural variables.

children.title: Spontaneity and equilibrium criteria
children.description: Free energy gives a quantitative criterion for whether a process can proceed.

topics.title: Chemical Potential and Partial Molar Quantities
topics.description: Chemical potential is the central quantity linking thermodynamics to mixtures, phase equilibrium, reactions, and transport.

children.title: Chemical potential
children.description: Students learn chemical potential as escaping tendency and molar free energy in context.

children.title: Dependence on T, P, and composition
Partial molar properties
children.description: Mixtures require composition-sensitive quantities rather than simple pure-component molar values.

children.title: Fugacity and activity
children.description: Real systems need corrected measures of effective pressure and concentration.

topics.title: Phase Equilibria and Phase Diagrams
topics.description: Phase equilibrium connects chemical potential to real materials: boiling, freezing, polymorphs, mixtures, and critical behavior.

children.title: One-component phase diagrams
children.description: Students learn how pressure and temperature determine stable phases.

children.title: Clapeyron and Clausius-Clapeyron equations
children.description: These equations quantify phase-boundary slopes and vapor-pressure behavior.

children.title: Multicomponent phase behavior
children.description: Mixtures introduce composition as a variable and explain distillation and miscibility.

topics.title: Solutions, Mixing, and Nonideal Behavior
topics.description: Solutions are where molecular interactions become thermodynamic quantities, from colligative effects to activity models.

children.title: Ideal and real solutions
children.description: Students learn when simple mixing laws work and what deviations mean molecularly.

children.title: Colligative properties
children.description: Colligative effects show how chemical potential changes with solute concentration.

children.title: Electrolyte solutions
children.description: Charged solutions require special treatment because long-range interactions matter.

topics.title: Chemical Equilibrium
topics.description: Chemical equilibrium turns free energy minimization into reaction composition, equilibrium constants, and measurable chemical predictions.

children.title: Equilibrium constants
children.description: Students connect thermodynamic activities to the familiar K expression.

children.title: Temperature and pressure dependence
children.description: Equilibria shift with external conditions in quantitatively predictable ways.

children.title: Coupled equilibria
children.description: Real chemistry often involves linked acid-base, solubility, redox, or binding equilibria.

topics.title: Electrochemical Thermodynamics
topics.description: Electrochemistry is free energy made electrical, and it gives a powerful laboratory route to thermodynamic data.

children.title: Cell potentials and Gibbs energy
children.description: Students learn how voltage measures chemical driving force.

children.title: Nernst equation
children.description: The Nernst equation connects composition and electrical potential.

children.title: Batteries and corrosion
children.description: Applications make thermodynamics concrete in materials, energy storage, and analytical chemistry.

topics.title: Statistical Mechanics Foundations
topics.description: Statistical mechanics explains thermodynamic laws from molecular states, probabilities, and energy levels.

children.title: Microstates and macrostates
children.description: Students learn how many microscopic arrangements correspond to one macroscopic state.

children.title: Ensembles
children.description: Ensembles formalize which variables are fixed and how probability is assigned.

children.title: Ergodicity and averages
children.description: Students connect molecular averages to experimentally measured thermodynamic quantities.

topics.title: Boltzmann Distribution and Molecular Populations
topics.description: The Boltzmann distribution is the bridge from energy levels to populations, spectroscopy, heat capacities, and reaction probabilities.

children.title: Canonical probability
children.description: Students learn why lower-energy states are more populated but higher-energy states matter at finite temperature.

children.title: Population ratios
children.description: Population ratios give direct insight into spectroscopy and molecular excitation.

children.title: Equipartition and limits
children.description: Students learn when classical energy sharing works and where quantum effects appear.

topics.title: Partition Functions and Molecular Thermodynamics
topics.description: Partition functions are compact engines for computing thermodynamic properties from molecular energy levels.

children.title: Molecular partition functions
children.description: Students learn to build translational, rotational, vibrational, and electronic contributions.

children.title: Thermodynamic properties from q and Q
children.description: This unit shows how energy, entropy, pressure, and free energy emerge from partition functions.

children.title: Chemical equilibrium from partition functions
children.description: Partition functions give equilibrium constants a molecular basis.

topics.title: Kinetic Theory, Transport, and Molecular Motion
topics.description: Kinetic theory connects molecular speeds and collisions to pressure, temperature, viscosity, diffusion, and reaction environments.

children.title: Maxwell-Boltzmann speeds
children.description: Students learn the distribution of molecular speeds and its temperature dependence.

children.title: Most probable, mean, and rms speeds
Transport properties
children.description: Transport links microscopic motion to macroscopic fluxes.

children.title: Collision models
children.description: Collision concepts prepare students for kinetics and reaction-rate theory.

topics.title: Fluctuations, Phase Transitions, and Critical Phenomena
topics.description: A world-class course should show where thermodynamics meets collective behavior: fluctuations, cooperative transitions, and limits of mean behavior.

children.title: Thermodynamic fluctuations
children.description: Students learn that fluctuations shrink in large systems but matter in small and critical systems.

children.title: Phase transitions
children.description: Phase transitions reveal nonanalytic behavior and collective molecular organization.

children.title: Critical phenomena preview
children.description: Students see why behavior near critical points is universal and subtle.

topics.title: Data, Computation, and Experimental Thermodynamics
topics.description: The final unit helps students use thermodynamics like practicing chemists: with real data, uncertainty, models, and computational checks.

children.title: Thermochemical data
children.description: Students learn to find, interpret, and use authoritative property data.

children.title: Computational thermodynamics
children.description: Simple computation makes nonlinear equilibria and phase behavior tractable.

children.title: Model validation and uncertainty
children.description: Students learn to question results and communicate confidence.
